title: Evaluation pilot project intensive care 3+1
summary: The shortage of qualified nurses, especially in intensive care, is a growing problem. This can lead to inadequate care for patients in need of intensive care and a high level of dissatisfaction among nurses. Several factors contribute to this problem, including the increasing number of older patients and the departure of qualified nurses due to high workloads and also older age. Critical care requires specialized knowledge and experience. The shortage of qualified nurses threatens the quality of healthcare, especially in the face of future challenges such as demographic change and climate change. The "Intensive Care 3+1" pilot project in Baden-Württemberg offers nurses the opportunity to enter further intensive care training directly after their generalist vocational training. This model is intended to shorten the training path and attract and retain more qualified nurses. The aim of the pilot project is to compare the skills and competencies of graduates of "3+1" continuing education with those of conventional continuing education. In the planned study, data will be collected at three points in time: before "Intensive Care 3+1" continuing education begins, when it is completed, and then again twelve months after completion. Data will be collected through various tests, questionnaires, and opinions of participants and their supervisors. Group interviews will also be conducted with ward managers* and faculty in the field. The results of this study will show whether the graduates of the "Intensive Care 3+1" project are as good as those who did the traditional intensiv care training. If so, this could open a new path for young nurses and help to reduce the nursing shortage in ICUs in the long term.
conditions: Competencies of nurses, attitudes toward a new educational program/pathway
